newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary o/n rates rise to end at 20.375 percent.
newsitem.headline: Hungary o/n rates rise to end at 20.375 percent.

text.p: Hungary's overnight rates continued to edge up on Friday and closed at 20.375 percent, up from Thursday's closing 20 percent, dealers said.
Dealers said that substantial funds flowed into reverse repo deals with the central bank on Tuesday, the last day of the commercial banks' previous two-week reserve period.
"The market went down to 19.25 levels then and there are some large banks which do not like lending at such low rates," said Sandor Tolonics of Commerzbank.

The banks can lend money to the central bank at 20 percent for one week and 20.50 percent for one month, and larger banks have enough liquidity to lend for one month on the interbank market if the interest rate is favourable, Tolonics said.
Market liquidity was also reduced by tax payments, dealers said.

They added that a slow rise in the overnight rates may continue early next week and perhaps to as high levels as 20.50 percent, depending on how much money the banks placed in their obligatory reserves on Friday.
